title: Are Dental Assistants in Demand in New Jersey?
summary: Dental assistants are in demand across the country and in New Jersey job projections are nearly double the national average1
body_markdown:
Dental assistants are in demand across the country and in New Jersey job projections are nearly double the national average1. As more NJ residents seek preventive dental care, the state's population ages, and dental practices continue to expand, employers seek dental assistants to help deliver quality patient care. If you’re a people person who likes hands-on work and wants a real career, this healthcare field might be right for you. Check out what’s happening for New Jersey dental assistants.


## New Jersey Job Outlook for Dental Assistants


New Jersey is home to thousands of dental offices and clinics, supporting employment opportunities for qualified dental assistants across the state. Employment of dental assistants in the state is projected to grow faster than the average, with nearly 1,600 dental assistant job openings each year through the decade1.


## Where Do Dental Assistants Work in New Jersey?


From general dentistry offices to orthodontic practices and oral surgery centers, dental assistants can find career opportunities throughout New Jersey in large and small communities. areas include major population centers such as:


- Newark
- Jersey City
- Paterson
- Elizabeth
- Edison
- Toms River
- Trenton
- Cherry Hill


Growing suburban communities throughout northern, central, and southern New Jersey help support employment opportunities for dental assistants in local dental practices. Regardless of where patients live, patients need prefer access to preventive dental care, creating opportunities for dental assistants across the state.


## Who Hires Dental Assistants in New Jersey?


Dental Assistants work in a variety of healthcare settings, including:


- General dentistry practices
- Pediatric dental offices
- Orthodontic practices
- Oral surgery offices
- Periodontal practices
- Endodontic offices
- Prosthodontic practices
- Community health clinics
- Dental service organizations
- Specialty dental centers


Because nearly every dental practice relies on dental assistants, graduates have the flexibility to pursue careers in different specialties throughout New Jersey. Among area employers often looking to hire are:


- [Aspen Dental Linden](https://www.aspendental.com/dentist/nj/linden/)
- [Da Vinci Dental Arts](https://www.davincidentalartsnj.com/)
- [Montgomery Dental Loft](https://www.montgomerydentalloft.com/)
- [Eastern Dental](https://www.easterndental.com/)
- [Smiles Dental](https://www.smiledentalnj.com/)


## Why Is Demand Up for Dental Assistants in New Jersey?


Demand for dental services exists nationwide, but several factors specifically shape the dental industry in the Garden State.


### New Jersey's Aging Population


As[New Jersey's population gets older](https://usafacts.org/answers/how-many-people-live-in-the-us/state/new-jersey/) , demand for dental care increases. Older adults often need restorative and specialized procedures, like crowns, bridges, implants, dentures, periodontal treatment, and oral surgery. Dental assistants help prepare patients, assist during procedures, and support efficient care delivery.


### New Jersey Residents Go to The Dentist


New Jerseyans buck the trend with[70 percent saying they’ve been to the dentist within the year](https://www.americashealthrankings.org/explore/measures/dental/NJ) . The[New Jersey Department of Health](https://www.nj.gov/health/fhs/oral/) also supports several children’s oral health initiatives designed to get kids on the right track including a “Sugar-Less Day to Prevent Tooth Decay" and a “Dial A Smile” reference tool that provides centralized information on public dental clinic services in the state. Because the state and its residents support good oral health, dental practices are busy and require dental assistants to be part of the team.


### NJ Dental Practices Are Expanding


Many New Jersey dental offices continue to add providers, expand office hours, adopt new technologies, and open additional locations to serve growing communities. Each expansion creates additional opportunities for trained dental assistants who can assist with[four-handed dentistry](https://www.lincolntech.edu/news/health-sciences/dental-assistant/what-is-four-handed-dentistry) and support both clinical and administrative operations.


### Experienced NJ Dental Professionals Are Retiring


Like many healthcare professions, dentistry is experiencing workforce turnover as experienced professionals retire. As longtime dental assistants leave the workforce, practices seek qualified new professionals to maintain patient care and office efficiency.


## Why Become a Dental Assistant in New Jersey?


There are plenty of[reasons to become a dental assistant in NJ](https://www.lincolntech.edu/news/health-sciences/dental-assistant/why-become-a-dental-assistant) . You can prepare for the career without spending years in school, work directly with patients every day, and build skills that are valuable across a wide range of dental specialties. New Jersey dental assistants also earn above the national average for the profession2.


Most importantly, you get to be part of a healthcare team providing essential services to a diverse group of patients. You literally help bring smiles to people’s faces!


## Attend[Dental Assistant School](https://www.lincolntech.edu/news/health-sciences/dental-assistant/what-look-dental-assistant-school) in New Jersey


Are you ready to[become a dental assistant](https://www.lincolntech.edu/news/health-sciences/dental-assistant/how-to-become-a-dental-assistant) ? Lincoln Tech's[Dental Assistant certificate program in Iselin, NJ](https://www.lincolntech.edu/campus/iselin-nj/programs/dental-assistant/certificate) provides hands-on training designed to prepare you to work in the modern dental practice. You learn all about clinical procedures, chairside assisting techniques, dental terminology, infection control, radiography concepts, and other practical skills used in modern dental offices.
